vulnerability.name: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm
vulnerability.description: braces through 3.0.3 lacks depth guards in its recursive AST walkers, so a deeply nested brace pattern under the character limit exhausts the call stack and terminates the Node.js process with an uncaught RangeError.

statements.impact_statement: The advisory's vulnerable range is `<= 3.0.3` and 3.0.3 is the highest version ever published (npm registry, read 2026-10-16), so no upgrade or override target exists; GitHub reports first_patched: NONE. braces reaches this repository through exactly one path, micromatch 4.0.8 <- starlight-llms-txt 0.12.0, a dependency of apps/docs, the private docs-site workspace, and that path never calls it. micromatch calls braces only from micromatch.parse, micromatch.braces and micromatch.braceExpand; starlight-llms-txt calls only micromatch.isMatch (generator.ts), which routes to picomatch 2.3.2, a package with no dependencies. Measured 2026-10-16: the docs build (`pnpm run build` in apps/docs) ran green under an in-package call logger appended to braces/index.js and micromatch/index.js; one process loaded both modules and made zero calls into braces, the logger having been positive-controlled against micromatch.braces('x/{a,b}') first. The patterns that reach isMatch are the plugin's include, exclude, promote and demote globs from astro.config.ts, authored in this repository, so no attacker-supplied pattern reaches the matcher even if a future micromatch path did expand braces. The published `memhtml` package is assembled from packages/* by scripts/package-manifest.mjs, which excludes apps/docs, so braces ships to no user. Revisit if starlight-llms-txt or another docs dependency starts expanding brace patterns from page content or user input, or if a braces release above 3.0.3 appears.
